content.title: OKC Thunder cruises past Lakers, inches closer to securing West's top seed
content.text: April 7, 2026Updated April 8, 2026, 4:02 p.m. CTThe OKC Thunder defeated a short-handed Los Angeles Lakers team 123-87 Tuesday night at Crypto.com Arena.Shai Gilgeous-Alexander led the Thunder with 25 points and eight assists in 28 minutes.OKC can secure the top seed in the Western Conference with a win on Wednesday night against the Clippers.Former Gonzaga teammates Chet Holmgren and Drew Timme faced off, with Holmgren recording a double-double.LOS ANGELES — The OKC Thunder's most important game is the one that's next on the schedule.That's something the team often says. And while it's easy to put that into words, putting it into action is a bit more challenging. Especially on a night like Tuesday, when OKC faced a short-handed Los Angeles Lakers team that was a 15.5-point underdog.But the Thunder still showed concentration in a game where others would show complacency. It pulled away during the second quarter and never looked back, earning a 123-87 road win.Shai Gilgeous-Alexander led the charge with 25 points and eight assists, while Isaiah Joe added 18 points and two rebounds off the bench.“When there’s a team out there that you’re not used to seeing, you’ve got to calibrate a little bit with just how they’re gonna play and how they’re gonna attack," Thunder head coach Mark Daigneault said. "And that took us a minute, obviously, in the game. ... It was tied at 42 at one point, and then the group that finished the first half did a really good job of stringing together stops and quality possessions on offense."It gave us some cushion at halftime, and then we continued that in the second half.”OKC improved to 63-16 on the season with the win. And its next game, a road matchup with the Los Angeles Clippers at 9 p.m. CT Wednesday, may actually be its most important of the season.OKC can secure the top seed in the Western Conference with a win. It could also do so if the San Antonio Spurs lose their home game against the Portland Trail Blazers at 8:30 p.m.Here are three takeaways from the win:Order new book on Thunder's run to NBA titleChet Holmgren battled former Gonzaga teammate Drew TimmeStarters always dap each other up prior to the opening tipoff. It's customary in the NBA, and Chet Holmgren went through the motions by handing out some half-hearted handshakes to the Lakers' players.But there was one exception. It was Drew Timme, who played alongside Holmgren at Gonzaga in 2021-22. The former teammates were all smiles as they connected on a booming dap-up near halfcourt.Timme got the start on a night when Los Angeles was without Luka Doncic (left hamstring strain), LeBron James (left foot injury management), Austin Reaves (left oblique muscle strain), Marcus Smart (right ankle contusion) and Jaxson Hayes (left foot soreness). And the undrafted sophomore showed some of the skills that made him a three-time All American in college.Timme scored 10 of Los Angeles' first 15 points. He ultimately ended the night with 11 points, three rebounds and two assists in 26 minutes.But Holmgren also showed off some skills of his own. The All-Star forward recorded 15 points, 10 rebounds, two steals and two blocks in 22 minutes.“I’m extremely happy for him," Holmgren said of Timme. "He’s a helluva player and a helluva worker. I’m happy to see him get some opportunity and make the most of it out there. We were both extremely focused on the game, but lots of jokes going back and forth up and down the floor. I kind of learned (from Timme) how to be a professional when it comes down to being on the court. Obviously, Drew is very known for being a goofy and not-take-life-too-serious kind of guy."But when it came to basketball, he was all business with how he prepared for it and how he played the game. It was great to be able to watch that and learn from him. I’ve just tried to apply that to my journey.”Cason Wallace watched girlfriend Kiki Rice, UCLA women's basketball team get honored for NCAA titleKiki Rice proudly held up a Lakers jersey at halfcourt to show the text on the back."UCLA Champs," the jersey read where the player's last name usually goes, with No. 26 below it.Rice was honored on the court alongside her UCLA women's basketball teammates, who recently won the program's first NCAA championship, after the first quarter of Tuesday's contest. And while she waved Los Angeles' jersey, the senior guard was undoubtedly rooting for OKC.Her boyfriend is Thunder guard Cason Wallace, after all.“That was great," Wallace said of Rice's recent championship. "It was fun just seeing her live out her dreams. She was very excited and happy. She works every day. It’s a lot of work and she’s consistent with it, so for her to have those achievements and her hard work paying off is great.”Wallace proceeded to put up five points, three steals and three assists in 23 minutes off the bench. He then did a jersey swap with Rice, who was far more inclined to hold up some Thunder threads, after the game.Shai Gilgeous-Alexander sat out another fourth quarter after dominant performanceGilgeous-Alexander walked the ball up the floor late in the third quarter. He was conserving his energy before punching the gas pedal.Without any warning, the superstar guard blew past Kobe Bufkin and elevated toward the rim. Bronny James jumped but didn't jump higher than Gilgeous-Alexander, who threw down a two-handed dunk.Gilgeous-Alexander recorded his 25 points and eight assists in only 28 minutes. He went 10 for 15 from the field (2 for 2 from deep).Gilgeous-Alexander then continued to conserve his energy, as he sat out the entire fourth quarter of the blowout contest. It marked the 25th time he's done so this season.Tip-ins∎ Shai Gilgeous-Alexander has scored at least 20 points in 139 straight games. It's the longest streak in NBA history.∎ Mark Daigneault on the readiness of Jared McCain, who recorded 15 points in 16 minutes off the bench: “He’s done a nice job of just taking the opportunities that come and making the most of them, staying aggressive inside of those opportunities. He caught a nice rhythm tonight. I thought he was forceful, decisive and did a nice job. We’re going to obviously need everybody, and he’s certainly someone who has proven that he’s got utility to us, that can help us. So we’ve got to keep him confident and playing with his head down.”∎ OKC was without Thomas Sorber (right ACL surgical recovery) and Jalen Williams (right hamstring injury management).∎ Los Angeles was without Luka Doncic (left hamstring strain), Jaxson Hayes (left foot soreness), LeBron James (left foot injury management), Austin Reaves (left oblique muscle strain) and Marcus Smart (right ankle contusion).Justin Martinez covers the Thunder and NBA for The Oklahoman.
